title: Family support networks can extend beyond legal and household ties
source_unit: Pew Research Center survey of U.S. adults, including 4,271 Black adults, fielded June 16-29, 2025

denominator.unit: Black U.S. adults surveyed; comparison sample included in total survey

black_close_to_nonrelative_family.unit: percent among Black adults with such a person

black_close_to_partner.unit: percent among Black adults with a spouse or partner

black_close_to_parent.unit: percent among Black adults with a living parent

black_close_to_sibling.unit: percent among Black adults with a living sibling

black_close_to_grandparent.unit: percent among Black adults with a living grandparent; 33% among non-Black adults

black_close_to_cousin.unit: percent among Black adults with a living cousin; 20% among non-Black adults

black_close_to_aunt_uncle.unit: percent among Black adults with a living aunt or uncle; 19% among non-Black adults

observations.method: Pew Research Center survey of 6,871 U.S. adults, including 4,271 Black adults, using the American Trends Panel and SSRS Opinion Panel; closeness measures are conditional on having the named relationship.
observations.uncertainty: This is a cross-sectional survey of reported closeness and family definition. It does not measure delivered care, financial transfers, household co-residence, burden, or causal effects. Relationship-specific denominators differ.
observations.subgroup: Black adults compared with non-Black adults; family includes birth, marriage, law, and chosen/non-relative ties as defined by the survey.
observations.counterinterpretation: Broad family recognition and closeness can provide support, but can also coexist with obligation, unequal labor, conflict, distance, or limited material capacity.

related_sources.claim: Pew report materials provide the questionnaire, topline, methodology, and detailed family-network analysis.

boundary: This record adds a cultural and social-network layer: family can be defined through birth, law, marriage, and choice, with reported closeness extending beyond the nuclear household. It does not establish care delivery, financial support, burden, household security, identity causation, trust, political action, or later durability.
